title: UConn Stuns Duke for First National Title
dek: Nine-and-a-half-point underdogs, UConn snapped Duke's 32-game winning streak, 77-74, as Ricky Moore's defense forced Trajan Langdon into a travel with 5.4 seconds left.

tip.text: 9:18 p.m. ET (listed start; the Courant put the final buzzer at 11:27 p.m.)

setup.text: Duke arrived in St. Petersburg as the sport's juggernaut: 37-1, unbeaten through the Atlantic Coast Conference, winners of 32 straight and the nation's highest-scoring team, led by national player of the year Elton Brand and senior sharpshooter Trajan Langdon.

Connecticut was 33-2 and had spent 10 weeks at No. 1. Its only losses came to Syracuse, with Richard Hamilton and Jake Voskuhl out injured, and to Miami. Hamilton, an All-American, had passed up the NBA the previous spring to chase a title.

Still, the Huskies were 9½-point underdogs, a spread the Courant called the highest in eight years. Jim Calhoun was coaching in his first Final Four after three regional-final losses at UConn, including the 1990 East final, decided by Christian Laettner's overtime buzzer-beater for Duke.

Duke and UConn were the only teams to hold the No. 1 ranking that season, and they met with a combined 70-3 record. The UConn players had said they would rather face Duke than Michigan State, and before the game Khalid El-Amin told CBS's Bonnie Bernstein the Huskies planned to shock the world.

game.text: Duke struck first, building a 9-2 lead a little more than three minutes in. Then Ricky Moore, UConn's senior defensive specialist, went on the attack, scoring nine points in a 15-4 run that put the Huskies up 17-13. He had all 13 of his points by halftime.

The first half brought seven ties and six lead changes. UConn led 36-32 with 1:28 left before Langdon answered with two 3-pointers over Moore, the second with 24.1 seconds left and a foul for a four-point play. Duke went to the locker room ahead 39-37.

Langdon's jumper and another 3 helped Duke edge ahead 48-43 early in the second half. Hamilton answered with nine points in six minutes, and his 18-footer off a screen made it 65-59, UConn's largest lead, with just under nine minutes to play.

Then Elton Brand took over, blocking shots and finishing a fast break, while UConn went more than four minutes without a field goal. Chris Carrawell's jumper tied it at 66, and El-Amin ended the drought with a short jumper for a 68-66 lead.

sequence.text: Trajan Langdon makes two free throws to tie it at 68. It is the 14th and last tie of the night.
Richard Hamilton answers with two free throws. UConn will not trail again.
UConn goes back to its press, and Duke turns the ball over before setting up. Hamilton buries a 23-foot 3-pointer from the left wing.
After a Carrawell free throw and a UConn turnover, Shane Battier grabs an offensive rebound and kicks it out to Langdon, whose long 3 pulls Duke within a point.
Khalid El-Amin drives past Brand on a switch and floats a shot over Battier.
Moore fouls William Avery, who makes both free throws. They are Duke's last points.
El-Amin's running shot in the lane misses. Chris Carrawell rebounds, and Mike Krzyzewski chooses not to call timeout, putting the ball in Langdon's hands.
Langdon takes Moore on the right wing, dribbles between his legs, spins into the lane and is called for traveling.
Duke fouls El-Amin on the inbounds pass, and he makes both free throws.
Again without a timeout, Langdon pushes upcourt into El-Amin and Rashamel Jones, falls and loses the ball as time runs out. Jones scoops it up. UConn is national champion.

quotes.when: at the final buzzer, shouted at the national TV audience

quotes.text: On that last play, I knew he was going to come at me. But I knew my will to win was going to take over and it did.
quotes.when: postgame, on the final Duke possession

quotes.text: I'll win or lose with Trajan Langdon. I'll walk down any road with Trajan Langdon.
I just wanted to make a move. I wasn't thinking about the clock. I might have traveled, I might not have. That's the way the game goes.

aftermath.text: Hamilton, who scored 27, was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player, and Moore made the all-tournament team. UConn fans chanted for Hamilton to stay one more year; instead he was the seventh pick in the 1999 NBA draft, by Washington.

In Storrs, students who watched at Gampel Pavilion streamed to a university-sanctioned bonfire. Early Tuesday, after bottles were thrown at police and firefighters at a later bonfire, 15 people were arrested; officials said at least 11 were not UConn students.

The next day about 7,000 fans met the team's charter at Bradley International Airport, an estimated 50,000 lined the 35-mile route to Storrs, and more than 12,000 packed Gampel for a rally while 3,000 more were turned away.
On April 17 a victory parade through downtown Hartford drew at least 175,000 people, by a Hartford police estimate; state Capitol police put the crowd at 250,000 to 270,000.

legacy.text: Looking back in 2020, the Associated Press called the win the one that vaulted UConn into college basketball's top tier, with three more titles in the next 15 seasons.
It was the first of the six national championships listed in UConn's record book: 1999, 2004, 2011, 2014, 2023 and 2024.
El-Amin's line outlived the night. When UConn won again in 2004, the Courant's columnist was still quoting him, and in a WTIC radio countdown of its top 10 UConn games this one ranked No. 1.
